subject: Production: out-of-order stream frames causing increased latency and 5xx errors
messages:
From: Tomas Weber <tomas@clearmaptech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: support@clearmaptech.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production incident: spikes in latency and 502s (samples attached)

Hi Soojin —

We started seeing a big uptick in errors at ~07:40 PDT this morning. Our frontend teams see intermittent 502/504s and sustained tail latency (>2s) for streaming responses to user sessions. We attached two snippets: sample_request.txt (the original request payload) and trace_snippet.log (server-side traces showing back-to-back stream frame reorder and parser exceptions).

This is high-impact — it is affecting search results in our live product. Can you confirm this is on your side or if something changed in our integration? We rolled no SDK changes.

Requesting an urgent triage and an incident call if needed.

Attachments: sample_request.txt (text), trace_snippet.log (text)

Thanks,
Tomas
CTO, ClearMap Tech
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Tomas Weber <tomas@clearmaptech.com>

Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 08:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production incident: spikes in latency and 502s (samples attached)

Tomas — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. We take production impact very seriously.

I've looped in Dev (runtime/inference) and Marissa (CS) to coordinate. Initial plan:
- Dev will triage immediately for streaming parser errors and any mismatches between gateway and client framing.
- Marissa will prepare a short status note for your execs.
- We'll open an incident channel and share updates every 30–60 minutes until resolved.

Can you confirm the SDK version you're running and whether you had any proxy or edge changes this morning? Also, if you can share a low-noise sample traffic window (start/end timestamps) that'll speed repro.

I'll keep you posted.

— Soojin
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Tomas Weber <tomas@clearmaptech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production incident: spikes in latency and 502s (samples attached)

We're on it. Quick notes from an initial pass:
- The trace shows the server receiving stream frames where the final trailer/frame ordering is inconsistent with our expected sequence for chunked streaming. Parser exceptions line up with the times Tomas reported.
- This looks like a client-side streaming framing mismatch; there is an open SDK bug (refs below) where under certain proxy backpressure conditions the client will emit two small frames out-of-order when the connection experiences a stall.
- Repro steps are small but consistent on our internal harness; prepping a minimal repro now.

Immediate mitigations we can push:
1) Gatekeeper fallback: route production traffic for ClearMap to the conservative parser that tolerates out-of-order frames (short-term, config change on our gateway).
2) Hotfix to SDK: patch client framing to serialize final trailer frames (we have a PR drafted, can fast-track release to npm/pypi in 1–2 hours if approved).
3) Circuit-breaker: temporarily enable stricter per-connection concurrency limits for affected routes to reduce backpressure.

Attachments: repro_harness.tar.gz (stub)
Related issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/789

I'll start a private build and ping when we have a candidate. If we push the gateway fallback first, we can buy time for an SDK release.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Tomas Weber <tomas@clearmaptech.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production incident: spikes in latency and 502s (samples attached)

Tomas — we'll get a working mitigation in place ASAP. For the exec call, draft talking points below (also attached as talking_points.md):
- What happened: client SDK + proxy backpressure caused out-of-order stream frames; Redwood parser threw exceptions leading to increased 5xxs and tail latency.
- What we're doing: apply gateway fallback to tolerant parser (now), release SDK patch (1–2 hours), optional credit if SLA threshold breached during incident.
- ETA: initial mitigation in 20–30 minutes, SDK release in 1–2 hours, full resolution once client upgrades (we will help coordinate).

Can you confirm whether ClearMap will want a joint post-mortem and whether you want our engineering leads on the exec call?

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick attention. We're still seeing errors in the 09:30–09:40 window; tail latency remains high and a small but important subset of user sessions get stuck waiting for streaming results. We've flagged this to our product/ops and they are considering pausing the rollout if it continues.

Please escalate to Redwood execs — our CEO is on standby and wants a direct timeline. If ClearMap misses an SLO because of this, we'll need compensation; please include billing in the loop. We need the gateway fallback now and a clear upgrade path for our clients.

Subject: Re: Production incident: spikes in latency and 502s (samples attached)

Vivek / leadership — escalating for visibility. Summary and action plan below for exec review and approval:

Summary: ClearMap (large US customer, DEAL-3341) observed increased latency and 5xx errors starting 2026-09-19 07:40 PDT caused by out-of-order stream frames from the client path which trigger our streaming parser to fail under specific proxy backpressure conditions.

Immediate actions taken:
- Gateway fallback: configured to use tolerant parser for ClearMap routing (deployed 09/19 10:05 PDT) — mitigated the spike in 5xxs but not yet fully eliminated tail latency for in-progress sessions.
- Engineering: Dev has a repro and a PR for the SDK patch; private builds are ready and we can publish a hotfix within 1–2 hours pending release approval.
- CS/Commercial: Marissa has prepped exec talking points and a temporary credit offer if SLA is breached.

Request from leadership:
1) Approve immediate hotfix publish and notify security/release for expedited rollout.
2) Approve offering a one-time credit (suggest 10%) if ClearMap measures an SLO breach during the incident window.
3) Nominate execs for a joint post-mortem (we propose Vivek + CTO-level eng representative).

Customer impact: production queries affected intermittently; ClearMap is considering pausing a rollout without a quick resolution. This is time-sensitive.

I'll coordinate a 30-minute incident briefing with leadership and the customer once we have a confirmed SDK build.

— Soojin
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
